source.preliminary: Cambridge B1 Preliminary Vocabulary List August 2025

words.definition: used when you compare two things that are the same in some way (as tall as)
words.definitionVi: được sử dụng khi bạn so sánh hai thứ giống nhau ở một khía cạnh nào đó (cao bằng)
words.hint: Use 'as' with another 'as' to compare things: 'as tall as'.
words.fact: You often see 'as' twice in one sentence, like 'as fast as a cheetah'.
sentences: Sam is as tall as his brother.
This bag is as heavy as that one.
Please speak as quietly as you can.
Mia can run as fast as Leo.
The film was as funny as the book.
Try to write as neatly as Ana.
Today is as cold as yesterday.
Don't shout as loudly as that!
Is your room as big as mine?
We played as carefully as we could.

words.definition: used to say two things are the same in some way
words.definitionVi: cấu trúc so sánh bằng, nghĩa là 'bằng như'
words.hint: Try it: 'She is as tall as her brother.'
words.fact: This pattern helps you compare people, animals, or things easily.
sentences: Ben is as strong as Tom.
This puzzle is as hard as the last one.
Please be as quiet as a mouse.
We finished as quickly as we could.
Mia can swim as well as her sister.
Listen as carefully as you can.
My bag is as light as yours.
Don't run as fast as that indoors!
Is the test as easy as you thought?
Children learn as much as they can with games.

words.definition: a person who travels and works in space
words.definitionVi: phi hành gia, người bay vào vũ trụ
words.hint: Astronauts wear a special suit and helmet in space.
words.fact: Astronauts float because there is very little gravity in space.
sentences: Tom wants to be an astronaut one day.
The astronaut floated inside the spaceship.
We watched a film about an astronaut.
Emma drew an astronaut in her picture.
Astronauts wear special suits in space.
Can you see the astronaut on TV?
The astronaut talked to children at school.
I read a book about an astronaut.
We learned how astronauts eat in space.
Would you like to meet an astronaut?

words.definition: right now, at this exact time
words.hint: Use it to say what is happening now: 'I am reading at the moment.'
words.fact: 'At the moment' is a handy phrase for talking about now in English.
sentences: I can't play at the moment — I'm busy.
Tom is doing his homework at the moment.
Please wait; Mum is on the phone at the moment.
We are staying at home at the moment.
Leo can't run at the moment because his leg hurts.
Listen carefully; the teacher is speaking at the moment.
I am writing a story at the moment.
Don't go out at the moment — it's raining.
Can you help me at the moment?
The children are learning a song at the moment.

words.definition: the season between summer and winter when leaves fall
words.definitionVi: mùa thu, mùa giữa hè và đông
words.hint: Leaves turn orange and brown in autumn.
words.fact: Autumn is also called 'fall' in American English.
sentences: I like autumn because the leaves change colour.
Emma plays football in autumn.
Look at the autumn leaves on the ground!
We talk about autumn in class.
Ben draws autumn trees.
Don't go out without a coat in cold autumn weather.
Autumn is windy today.
Can you feel the cool autumn air?
I wear a coat in autumn.
What is autumn like in your country?

words.definition: not in the usual place, or moving from a place
words.definitionVi: đi xa, không ở đây nữa
words.hint: Say 'run away' when someone leaves quickly.
words.fact: Birds fly away to warmer places in winter.
sentences: Please put the toys away.
Ana is away on holiday this week.
Go away — I'm doing my homework!
We played away from the busy road.
Noah can run away very fast.
Don't look away in class.
I threw the ball away by mistake.
Don't go away yet — stay and talk.
Can you move away from the door?
The children ran away when they heard the loud noise.

words.definition: to think the same as someone else
words.hint: Nod your head to show you agree.
words.fact: Friends do not always agree, and that is okay!
sentences: I agree with you about the story.
Mia agrees that the film was funny.
Please say if you agree.
Let's agree on a time to meet.
Ana agrees with her friend.
We all agree that Friday is best.
Do you agree with me?
Watch — they all agree!
Do you agree about the rules at home?
My teacher asked if we agree.

words.definition: the gas all around us that we breathe
words.definitionVi: không khí, thứ ta hít thở
words.hint: You cannot see air, but you can feel the wind.
words.fact: Air is made mostly of a gas called nitrogen.
sentences: The air outside feels cold today.
Ben likes fresh air in the park.
Open the window for some air!
We need clean air to stay healthy.
Leo breathes the cool air by the sea.
Can you feel the warm air?
Don't pollute the air.
The air smells sweet after the rain.
There is fresh air near the river.
My favourite thing in nature is clean air.

words.definition: a place where planes take off and land
words.definitionVi: sân bay, nơi máy bay cất và hạ cánh
words.hint: You check in your bags before you get on a plane at the airport.
words.fact: Some airports are so big that people travel between gates by train.
sentences: We went to the airport by bus.
Ben likes watching planes at the airport.
Look at that big airport!
We saw the airport from the taxi.
Ana drew an airport in her notebook.
Can you hear the planes at the airport?
Don't run inside the airport.
My dad drove us to the airport.
The airport is very busy today.
We travel from the airport to another country.

words.definition: without any other person near you
words.definitionVi: một mình, không có ai bên cạnh
words.hint: Being alone for a little while can feel peaceful.
words.fact: Some animals, like tigers, like to live alone.
sentences: I feel alone today.
Tom looks alone in the playground.
Don't leave your little sister alone.
Don't be alone if you feel sad — talk to someone.
Lily is alone in the classroom.
This story is about a boy who is alone.
My friend feels very alone.
Why do you feel alone?
We all feel alone sometimes.
Come and sit with us — you look alone.

words.definition: before now, or sooner than expected
words.hint: Say 'I have already finished' when a job is done early.
words.fact: 'Already' shows something happened faster than we thought!
sentences: I have already finished my homework.
Sam already knows the answer.
Please sit down — the lesson has already started.
We have already played in the park.
Zoe can already ride a bike.
Listen — I already told you in class.
I have already written three pages.
Don't go yet — I've already packed your bag.
Have you already done it?
Children already know many of these games.

words.definition: as well as something else already said
words.hint: Use 'also' to add more information: 'I like cats. I also like dogs.'
words.fact: 'Also', 'too', and 'as well' all mean almost the same thing.
sentences: Please do your writing, and also check the spelling.
Ben works hard and also helps his friends.
Speak clearly, and also listen carefully.
We play football and also basketball in the park.
Leo can run fast and also jump high.
Listen to the teacher and also write notes.
I write stories and also draw pictures.
Don't forget your book, and also bring a pencil.
Can you do it, and also help me?
Children learn English and also have fun with games.

words.definition: very surprising and wonderful
words.hint: Say 'amazing' when something is much better than you expected.
words.fact: Fireworks and rainbows often make people say 'amazing!'
sentences: I feel amazing today!
Mia looks amazing in her new dress.
What an amazing day!
Don't miss this amazing film.
Ana is amazing at football.
This story is amazing.
My friend is an amazing singer.
Why do you look so amazing?
We all had an amazing time.
Smile — you look amazing!

words.definition: a vehicle that takes sick or hurt people to hospital
words.hint: An ambulance has a loud siren and flashing lights.
words.fact: Ambulances can drive fast through red lights in an emergency.
sentences: I can see an ambulance in the picture.
An ambulance came to help the man.
Look! There is an ambulance.
We learned about ambulances at school today.
Sam pointed to an ambulance and waved.
Can you draw an ambulance, please?
Please make room for the ambulance.
The ambulance drove to the hospital quickly.
Leo found an ambulance in the book.
We talked about ambulances in class.

words.definition: in, at, or to any place
words.hint: Say 'anywhere' when the place does not matter: 'Sit anywhere you like.'
words.fact: You use 'anywhere' mostly in questions and negative sentences.
sentences: You can sit anywhere you like.
Ben can work anywhere with his laptop.
People can hear you anywhere if you shout.
We can play anywhere in the park.
Leo can run anywhere on the field.
Don't leave your bag anywhere in class.
I can't find my book anywhere.
Don't go anywhere without telling Mum.
Can you do your homework anywhere?
Children can learn anywhere with good games.

words.definition: to start to be seen
words.hint: A rainbow can appear after it rains.
words.fact: Magicians often make things appear and disappear as a trick.
sentences: A rainbow appeared in the sky after the rain.
Lily likes when stars appear at night.
Please wait — the answer will appear on the board.
Let's watch the moon appear.
Noah saw a bird appear behind the tree.
Dark clouds appear every afternoon.
Can you make a rabbit appear in the magic show?
Watch me make the coin appear!
Do strange noises appear at home at night?
My teacher asked when spring flowers appear.

words.definition: to get to a place at the end of a journey
words.hint: You arrive at school after your journey there.
words.fact: Trains and planes have a special time when they should arrive.
sentences: I arrive at school at eight o'clock.
Ana likes to arrive early.
Please arrive carefully and quietly.
Let's arrive together at the cinema.
Tom can arrive on time every day.
We arrive home after football.
Can you arrive before me, please?
Watch me arrive on my new bike!
Do you arrive home before dinner?
My teacher asked us to arrive early tomorrow.

words.definition: the subject where you draw, paint, and make things
words.hint: In art class you might paint a picture or make a model.
words.fact: Famous paintings are kept safe in places called art galleries.
sentences: I have art at school on Mondays.
Ben has his art book in his bag.
Please open your art book.
We need paints for the art lesson.
Lily writes her name on her art.
Can you give me the art materials?
Don't lose your art homework.
My teacher shows famous art.
I like this art.
Put your art on the desk.

words.definition: a person who makes paintings or other art
words.hint: An artist often uses a brush and paint.
words.fact: Some artists paint pictures, and some make statues or music.
sentences: Mia wants to be an artist one day.
The artist visited us at school.
We thanked the artist with a smile.
Leo drew an artist painting a picture.
That artist is very kind.
Can you see the artist at work?
The artist told us a story about her painting.
I like this artist's pictures.
We learn about artists in art class.
Say thank you to the artist.

words.definition: to perform a part in a play or film
words.hint: Actors act on a stage or in front of a camera.
words.fact: Children can act in school plays too!
sentences: I can act in the school play.
Ben likes to act in films.
Please act carefully on the stage.
Let's act this scene together.
Emma can act very well.
We act in drama class every week.
Can you act this part for me, please?
Watch me act like a lion!
Do you act in plays at home?
My teacher asked us to act the story.

words.definition: a person whose job is acting in films or plays
words.hint: An actor learns lines and pretends to be someone else.
words.fact: Actors sometimes wear costumes and make-up for their part.
sentences: Mia wants to be an actor one day.
The actor visited our school.
We thanked the actor with a smile.
Emma drew an actor on the stage.
That actor is kind to fans.
Can you see the actor on TV?
The actor read a story to the class.
I like that actor.
We learn about actors in English class.
Say thank you to the actor.

words.definition: used to say what is really true
words.hint: Use 'actually' to correct something: 'Actually, it's blue, not green.'
words.fact: 'Actually' helps you share a surprising true fact.
sentences: I can't come — actually, I have football.
Tom works hard; actually, he finished early.
Speak slowly — actually, wait a moment.
We play tennis; actually, we prefer football.
Lily can run fast; actually, she won the race.
Listen — actually, the answer is different.
I write stories; actually, this one is true.
Don't go yet — actually, Mum is calling.
Can you do it? Actually, let me help.
Children learn best with games — actually, that's true!

words.definition: an exciting journey or experience
words.hint: Storybooks about pirates or explorers are full of adventure.
words.fact: Going somewhere new can feel like a small adventure.
sentences: I can see an adventure story in the picture.
Emma had an adventure in the forest.
Look! Their adventure is starting.
We learned about a famous adventure at school.
Tom pointed to the adventure map and smiled.
Can you draw your favourite adventure, please?
Please tell me about your adventure.
My favourite thing is a good adventure.
Mia found an adventure story in the book.
We talked about adventures in class.

words.definition: later than something, or next in time
words.hint: You have a snack after school.
words.fact: 'After' tells you the order things happen in.
sentences: Please do it after lunch.
Ben works after school.
Speak after me, please.
We play after lessons in the park.
Leo can run after the ball.
Listen after the question in class.
I write after I read my book.
Don't go after dark.
Can you do it after me?
Children learn best after they rest.

words.definition: back in time from now
words.hint: Say 'two days ago' to talk about the past.
words.fact: 'Ago' always comes after the amount of time, like 'a week ago'.
sentences: I finished it two minutes ago.
Leo worked here a year ago.
She spoke to me a moment ago.
We played in the park an hour ago.
Sam could run faster a year ago.
Listen — I said that five minutes ago.
I wrote that page yesterday, not long ago.
Don't leave; Mum called two minutes ago.
Did you do it long ago?
Children learned this song a week ago.

words.definition: work of buying, selling, or making things for money
words.hint: A shop is a small kind of business.
words.fact: Some people start their own business when they grow up.
sentences: Emma wants to start a business one day.
The family business helps people in town.
We learned how a small business works.
Tom drew a shop for his business project.
My uncle's business is a bookshop.
Can you see the business on the corner?
The business sells fresh fruit.
I like learning about business at school.
We learn how businesses make money.
Say what kind of business you would like.

words.definition: a man who works in business, buying or selling things
words.hint: A businessman often wears a suit and carries a briefcase.
words.fact: Businessmen and businesswomen help run shops and companies.
sentences: Leo wants to be a businessman one day.
The businessman visited us at school.
We thanked the businessman for his talk.
Sam drew a businessman in a suit.
That businessman is kind to his workers.
Can you see the businessman at the meeting?
The businessman told us a story about his shop.
I like listening to the businessman.
We learn what a businessman does.
Say thank you to the businessman.

words.definition: a soft yellow food made from milk
words.hint: We spread butter on bread or toast.
words.fact: Butter is made by shaking or churning cream.
sentences: I like butter for lunch.
Emma eats butter at school.
Please give me some butter.
We buy butter at the shop.
Mia has butter at home.
Can you see butter in the picture?
Butter is my favourite food.
Mum puts butter on the table.
Don’t play with butter!
Let’s share the butter.

words.definition: a colourful insect with big, thin wings
words.hint: A butterfly starts life as a caterpillar.
words.fact: Butterflies taste with their feet, not their mouth!
sentences: I can see a butterfly in the garden.
Lily likes butterflies.
The butterfly is on the flower.
Can you draw a butterfly, please?
Noah has a book about butterflies.
Look at that butterfly!
We learn about butterflies at school.
Don't scare the butterfly.
Ben points to a butterfly in the picture.
My favourite insect is a butterfly.

words.definition: alone, with no one helping you
words.hint: Say 'I did it by myself' when you needed no help.
words.fact: Doing something by myself can make you feel proud.
sentences: Please let me do it by myself.
I work by myself at home.
I can speak by myself, thank you.
I play by myself in the park sometimes.
I can run by myself now.
I listen by myself with headphones.
I write by myself in my book.
I don't like going by myself.
Can I do it by myself?
I learned the song by myself.

words.definition: alone, without anyone else helping you
words.definitionVi: tự bạn, một mình bạn (làm gì)
words.hint: A teacher might say, 'Try it by yourself first.'
words.fact: Learning to do things by yourself helps you grow up.
sentences: Please do it by yourself.
Noah, can you work by yourself?
Speak by yourself, please — no reading from the paper.
You can play by yourself in the park.
Emma, can you run by yourself?
Listen by yourself and then answer.
Write the story by yourself in your book.
Don't go by yourself at night.
Can you do it by yourself?
Can you learn this by yourself with games?

words.definition: a bag you carry on your back
words.hint: You carry your books to school in a backpack.
words.fact: Backpacks have two straps so you can carry them on both shoulders.
sentences: I use a backpack at school.
Leo has a backpack in his locker.
Please open your backpack.
We need a backpack for the trip.
Mia puts books in her backpack.
Can you give me my backpack?
Don't lose your backpack.
My teacher shows us a new backpack.
I like this backpack.
Put your backpack under the desk.

words.definition: a strip of cloth used to cover a cut
words.hint: A nurse puts a bandage on a hurt knee or arm.
words.fact: Bandages keep a cut clean while it heals.
sentences: I can see a bandage in the picture.
Emma has a bandage on her finger.
Look! There is a clean bandage.
We learned how to put on a bandage at school.
Sam pointed to the bandage and smiled.
Can you draw a bandage, please?
Please show me how to use a bandage.
The nurse put a bandage on my knee.
Ana found a bandage in the first-aid box.
We talked about bandages in class.

words.definition: a place where people keep their money safe
words.hint: You can save your money in a bank.
words.fact: Banks also help people borrow money to buy a house.
sentences: We go to the bank on Saturday.
Lily likes visiting the bank with Dad.
There is a big bank near my house.
Can we go to the bank, please?
Mum puts money in the bank.
I can see the bank in the picture.
Don't run in the bank.
Meet me at the bank.
The bank closes at four o'clock.
We learn about the bank at school.

words.definition: a small insect with a hard, shiny back
words.hint: A beetle's hard wings protect its soft wings underneath.
words.fact: There are more kinds of beetles than any other animal on Earth.
sentences: I can see a beetle under the leaf.
Lily likes beetles.
The beetle is in the garden.
Can you draw a beetle, please?
Noah has a book about beetles.
Look at that beetle!
We learn about beetles at school.
Don't scare the beetle.
Emma points to a beetle in the picture.
My favourite insect is a beetle.

words.definition: earlier than something, or first in time
words.hint: Wash your hands before you eat.
words.fact: 'Before' is the opposite of 'after'.
sentences: Please do it before dinner.
Zoe works before school.
Speak before you write, please.
We play before lunch in the park.
Ben can run before the race starts.
Listen before you answer in class.
I write before I go to bed.
Don't go before I finish.
Can you do it before me?
Children learn better before they get tired.

words.definition: to start doing something
words.hint: The lesson will begin when the bell rings.
words.fact: 'Begin' and 'start' mean almost the same thing.
sentences: I can begin my homework at school.
Lily likes to begin early.
Please begin carefully.
Let's begin together.
Noah can begin the race very well.
We begin every day with a song.
Can you begin the game for me, please?
Watch me begin the story!
Do you begin your homework at home?
My teacher asked us to begin.

words.definition: to feel sure that something is true
words.hint: Say 'I believe you' when you trust what someone says.
words.fact: Many children believe in magic when they are young.
sentences: I believe we can win at school sports.
Sam likes to believe in magic stories.
Please believe me — I'm telling the truth.
Let's believe in our team together.
Leo can believe that hard work helps.
We believe every day gets better.
Can you believe this story?
Watch — they believe the news!
Do you believe in ghosts?
My teacher asked us to believe in ourselves.

words.definition: a strip you wear around your waist
words.hint: A belt keeps your trousers from falling down.
words.fact: In karate, belts of different colours show your skill level.
sentences: I wear a belt to school.
Ben puts on a belt.
Where is my belt?
Please wear your belt.
Leo has a new belt.
We put a belt in the bag.
Don’t lose your belt.
This belt is too small.
Can you find my belt?
I like my blue belt.

words.definition: a vehicle with two wheels that you pedal
words.hint: You need to balance carefully when you ride a bicycle.
words.fact: 'Bicycle' and 'bike' mean the same thing.
sentences: I go to school by bicycle.
Ben likes his new bicycle.
Look at that bicycle!
We see a bicycle in the street.
Ana draws a bicycle.
Can you ride a bicycle?
Don't run near the bicycle.
My dad rides a bicycle to work.
The bicycle is blue.
We travel by bicycle at the weekend.

words.definition: a container where you put rubbish
words.hint: Put your rubbish in the bin, not on the floor.
words.fact: Some bins are for recycling paper, plastic, or glass.
sentences: There is a bin in my kitchen.
Zoe puts paper in the bin.
Please empty the bin.
We have a bin at home.
Tom points to the bin.
Can you see a bin in the picture?
Don't jump on the bin.
My classroom has a recycling bin.
Mum buys a new bin for the house.
Look! There is a bin by the door.

words.definition: a small, flat, baked sweet snack
words.hint: You might dip a biscuit in milk or tea.
words.fact: In the US, a similar snack is called a 'cookie'.
sentences: I like a biscuit for lunch.
Mia eats a biscuit at school.
Please give me a biscuit.
We buy a biscuit at the shop.
Zoe has a biscuit in her bag.
Can you see a biscuit in the picture?
A biscuit is my favourite food.
Mum puts a biscuit on the table.
Don’t play with a biscuit!
Let’s share a biscuit.

words.definition: a small amount or small piece of something
words.hint: Say 'a bit tired' to mean a little tired.
words.fact: 'A bit' is a friendly way to say 'a little'.
sentences: I can see a bit of cake in the picture.
Tom has a bit of chocolate at home.
Look! There is a bit left.
We learned a bit about space at school today.
Leo ate a bit and smiled.
Can you wait a bit, please?
Please show me a bit of your drawing.
I'm a bit tired after the game.
Emma found a bit of paper in the book.
We talked a bit in class.

words.definition: feeling tired because there is nothing fun to do
words.hint: Find a game or a book when you feel bored.
words.fact: Being bored sometimes helps you think of fun new ideas.
sentences: I feel bored today.
Ana looks bored.
Don't sit there looking bored.
Don't be bored — let's play a game.
Tom is bored at the party.
This long lesson makes me bored.
My friend is very bored.
Why do you feel bored?
We all feel bored sometimes.
Smile — you look bored!

words.definition: to take something and give it back later
words.hint: You can borrow books from the library.
words.fact: Always remember to return what you borrow!
sentences: I can borrow a book at school.
Lily likes to borrow pencils.
Please borrow carefully and bring it back.
Let's borrow this game together.
Tom can borrow my ruler.
We borrow books every week.
Can I borrow this for a minute, please?
Watch me borrow a pen from the teacher!
Do you borrow books from the library?
My teacher asked us not to borrow without asking.

words.definition: a piece of jewellery worn around the wrist
words.hint: A bracelet can be made of beads, metal, or string.
words.fact: Friends sometimes make matching bracelets for each other.
sentences: I wear a bracelet to school.
Emma puts on a bracelet.
Where is my bracelet?
Please wear your bracelet.
Ben has a new bracelet.
We put a bracelet in the bag.
Don’t lose your bracelet.
This bracelet is too small.
Can you find my bracelet?
I like my blue bracelet.

words.definition: something built over a river or road so people can cross
words.definitionVi: cây cầu bắc qua sông hoặc đường để mọi người đi qua
words.hint: A bridge helps you cross a river without getting wet.
words.fact: Some famous bridges, like Tower Bridge, can open in the middle.
sentences: We walk across the bridge on Saturday.
Noah likes the old bridge.
There is a big bridge near my house.
Can we go to the bridge, please?
Zoe takes photos at the bridge.
I can see the bridge in the picture.
Don't run on the bridge.
Meet me at the bridge.
The bridge is very long.
We learn about bridges at school.

words.definition: damaged and in pieces, or not working
words.hint: A broken toy needs to be fixed or thrown away.
words.fact: If you drop a glass, it might get broken.
sentences: My phone is broken today.
Ana's toy looks broken.
What a broken window!
Don't use the broken chair.
Tom's pencil is broken.
This story book is broken — the pages are torn.
My friend's bike is badly broken.
Why is the TV broken?
We all have broken toys sometimes.
Careful — that cup looks broken!

words.definition: a tool with many small bristles, used for hair or cleaning
words.definitionVi: dụng cụ có nhiều sợi nhỏ, dùng chải tóc hoặc làm sạch
words.hint: You use a brush to tidy your hair or paint a picture.
words.fact: There are brushes for teeth, hair, paint, and even floors.
sentences: There is a brush in my bathroom.
Noah uses a brush on his hair.
Please clean the brush.
We have a brush at home.
Leo points to a paint brush.
Can you see a brush in the picture?
Don't throw the brush.
My favourite colour is on this brush.
Mum buys a new brush for the house.
Look! There is a brush by the sink.

words.definition: to damage something with fire or heat
words.hint: Be careful — the oven can burn your fingers.
words.fact: Fire fighters work hard to stop things from burning.
sentences: Don't burn your hand on the hot pan.
Ana's toast can burn if she waits too long.
Please be careful so you don't burn yourself.
The paper will burn in the fire.
Noah's finger will burn on that hot plate.
Dry leaves burn easily.
Can a candle burn for a long time?
Watch — the candle will burn slowly.
Do you ever burn toast at home?
My teacher told us never to play with fire or burn things.

words.definition: a chart that shows the days, weeks, and months
words.hint: Look at the calendar to find out what day your birthday is.
words.fact: A calendar has 12 months and about 365 days.
sentences: I mark my birthday on the calendar.
Mia checks the calendar every morning.
